# SpiralThinker: Latent Reasoning through an Iterative Process with Text–Latent Interleaving

- **Authors**: Shengmin Piao, Sanghyun Park
- **Venue**: ACL
- **Published**: unknown
- **Source**: anthology
- **Link**: <https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.1605/>
- **PDF**: <https://aclanthology.org/2026.findings-acl.1605.pdf>
- **DOI**: 10.18653/v1/2026.findings-acl.1605
- **Topics**: overthinking
- **Relevance score**: overthinking 0.40

## In one line

SpiralThinker interleaves explicit textual reasoning steps with implicit latent-token steps (rather than picking one mode exclusively, which the paper frames as risking overthinking in verbose textual frameworks or underthinking in purely latent ones), iteratively refining the latent representations across K passes with no new tokens generated, and stabilizes this via a progressive alignment objective that pulls each iteration's latent hidden state toward its corresponding explicit-reasoning-step hidden state (weighted to emphasize later, more consolidated iterations) -- beating five latent-reasoning baselines on GSM8K-Aug/ProsQA/StrategyQA, with ablations showing iteration alone can degrade performance and only iteration-plus-alignment together deliver the gains.

## Problem

Purely textual reasoning frameworks verbalize every step explicitly, risking either overthinking (excessive, redundant elaboration) or underthinking (insufficient exploration), while latent-reasoning approaches that compress reasoning into hidden representations sacrifice interpretability and controllability; existing latent-reasoning methods also lack mechanisms for stable, coherent reasoning dynamics in latent space (most treat latent representations as token-level inputs processed in a single forward pass, forcing them to encode entire reasoning steps at once without modeling how reasoning actually unfolds) and lack a systematic way to interleave implicit and explicit reasoning at the step level, the way human reasoning naturally alternates between internal thinking and external expression.

## Contributions

- SpiralThinker, a stabilized iterative latent reasoning framework that performs implicit reasoning through iterative refinement of latent representations while systematically interleaving it with explicit textual reasoning steps, addressing the interpretability/controllability loss of purely latent approaches and the overthinking/underthinking risks the paper attributes to purely textual frameworks
- a progressive alignment objective providing iteration-aware supervision that constrains latent representations to stay coherent with their corresponding explicit textual reasoning counterparts, using a softmax-based weighting schedule emphasizing later, more consolidated iterations while preserving earlier exploratory signal
- a structured text-latent interleaving training scheme (alternating explicit/latent steps) that lets the model autonomously learn when to transition between explicit and implicit reasoning during autoregressive generation
- state-of-the-art results among latent-reasoning baselines across mathematical, logical, and commonsense reasoning benchmarks, with ablations showing iteration alone can degrade performance and alignment alone gives only modest gains -- the combination of both mechanisms is what delivers the substantial, consistent improvement

## Method

Trains in two stages. (1) Explicit reasoning: fine-tunes the model on step-by-step reasoning with each step delimited by <bot>/<eot> boundary tokens, establishing fundamental stepwise reasoning capability and a foundation for the subsequent implicit stage. (2) Implicit reasoning: constructs an alternating text-latent training scheme where every reasoning step at odd or even positions is replaced by N <latent> tokens (delimited by <bol>/<eol>), so textual and latent reasoning coexist within the same sequence and the model learns transitions between the two modes; at iteration k (of K total), the hidden states at latent-token positions are extracted and transformed by a lightweight latent adapter g_phi (a residual MLP with RMSNorm and target-RMS scaling matched to the pretrained embedding distribution, addressing the mismatch between final-layer hidden-state and input-embedding subspaces), then written back into the embedding sequence to form an updated input for the next forward pass -- repeating this for K iterations enables continuous, deepening reasoning over latent representations with no new tokens generated. To keep these iterative latent updates meaningful and coherent (rather than drifting) rather than collapsing to noise, a progressive alignment objective constrains each latent representation's hidden state (at its <eol> position) to stay close (L1 distance, per-layer-normalized by a frozen-model-estimated scale) to the hidden state of the corresponding explicit textual reasoning step (at its <eot> position) from a frozen explicitly-trained reference model -- an intra-iteration alignment loss applied per iteration, then aggregated across all K iterations via a softmax-based weighting schedule that increases monotonically with iteration index, so later (more consolidated) iterations are emphasized more than earlier (more exploratory) ones, while still preserving some signal from earlier passes. The total training objective combines standard cross-entropy with this progressive alignment loss (weighted by lambda). At inference, N <latent> tokens are prepended before each textual step, and the model autonomously learns (from the alternating training scheme) to insert them at the right points, alternating implicit and explicit reasoning throughout generation via standard greedy autoregressive decoding.

## Results

Built on Llama-3.2-1B with LoRA fine-tuning, SpiralThinker consistently outperforms six latent-reasoning baselines (iCoT-KD, iCoT-SI, Token Assorted, Coconut, CODI, Pause Token) across all three evaluated reasoning benchmarks: 56.56% on GSM8K-Aug (math, +3.19 points over the previous best, Pause Token's 53.37%), 99.40% on ProsQA (logic, +0.40 over iCoT-SI's 99.00%), and 63.32% on StrategyQA (commonsense, +0.44 over iCoT-KD's 62.88%) -- the largest relative gain is on GSM8K-Aug, which the paper attributes to the iterative process particularly enhancing multi-step numerical reasoning, while the ProsQA gain (already near-ceiling for baselines) suggests better stability in high-accuracy regimes. Ablations isolating the iterative process and the alignment objective (Table 2) show: applying only the alignment objective (single-pass, no iteration) gives modest, consistent gains (+3.18/+0.60/+1.75 on the three benchmarks); applying only the iterative process (no alignment) gives limited improvement and can actively *degrade* performance on StrategyQA (-1.31), confirming that unconstrained iterative updates in latent space can drift rather than reliably improve reasoning; combining both mechanisms yields substantially larger, consistently positive gains (+11.07/+1.40/+3.93), confirming iteration and alignment play complementary roles -- iteration provides additional reasoning depth, while progressive alignment regulates this multi-step evolution to keep it structured, stable, and coherent, rather than either alone being sufficient. Sensitivity analysis of the number of latent tokens N (1 to 10) shows accuracy on GSM8K-Aug and ProsQA remains largely stable across the range, while StrategyQA accuracy decreases when N exceeds 6, indicating the optimal token count is dataset-dependent, consistent with prior latent-reasoning findings, with the best configuration being N=5 for GSM8K-Aug/ProsQA and N=6 for StrategyQA. Sensitivity analysis of iteration count K (1-6) shows a moderate number of iterations consistently improves accuracy, but excessive iteration leads to saturation or slight degradation (most notably on GSM8K-Aug and ProsQA), with the softmax-based weighting schedule for progressive alignment achieving the best results among three tested weighting strategies (uniform, last-iteration-only, softmax) -- uniform weighting consistently underperforms (most pronounced on ProsQA/StrategyQA), while softmax weighting achieves the highest peak accuracy on GSM8K-Aug/ProsQA and converges to its plateau with fewer iterations on StrategyQA, confirming that appropriately weighted alignment across iterations (emphasizing later, more consolidated passes while still retaining earlier exploratory signal) is important for effective iterative latent reasoning. A qualitative analysis of <latent> tokens (identifying which vocabulary tokens' embeddings are most similar to the latent representations across iterations, on a worked GSM8K-Aug example) shows the latent representations progressively refine toward numerically and semantically meaningful content as iterations proceed (e.g. converging toward digits relevant to the correct intermediate calculation), providing qualitative evidence that the iterative latent updates encode increasingly consolidated, interpretable reasoning content rather than opaque noise.

## Limitations

The optimal number of latent tokens N and iterations K are shown to be dataset-dependent rather than universal, requiring per-dataset tuning (e.g. N=5 for GSM8K-Aug/ProsQA vs. N=6 for StrategyQA; K=5/4/3 respectively for the three datasets under the softmax weighting schedule) rather than a single configuration transferring cleanly across tasks. Excessive iteration is shown to cause saturation or slight performance degradation on some benchmarks, so the iterative process requires care in setting K rather than simply maximizing it. Evaluation is conducted on a single, relatively small backbone (Llama-3.2-1B) with LoRA fine-tuning; generalization of the framework and its dataset-specific hyperparameter sensitivities to larger-scale models is not directly reported within the paper's own experiments.

## Why it matters here

- **overthinking**: Directly relevant: it explicitly names overthinking as a risk of purely textual reasoning frameworks that verbalize every step (paired with underthinking as the corresponding risk of purely latent approaches), and positions text-latent interleaving as a middle path that gets reasoning depth without paying full per-step token cost -- offering a distinct lever (moving reasoning computation into latent iterations rather than generated tokens) from the length-penalty, budget, or early-stopping mechanisms most other overthinking-mitigation papers in this archive use, while its ablation finding (unconstrained iteration alone can hurt, only alignment-plus-iteration together helps) is a specific caution for any method that adds extra computation to a reasoning process without a stabilizing supervision signal.

## Abstract

Recent advances in large reasoning models have been driven by reinforcement learning and test-time scaling, accompanied by growing interest in latent rather than purely textual reasoning. However, existing latent reasoning methods lack mechanisms to ensure stable reasoning dynamics in latent space and a systematic way to interleave implicit and explicit reasoning. We introduce SpiralThinker, a unified framework that performs iterative updates over latent representations while enabling interleaved reasoning across latent and textual steps. At its core, SpiralThinker employs a progressive alignment objective and structured annotations to stabilize latent reasoning and maintain coherence with textual reasoning. Across mathematical, logical, and commonsense reasoning tasks, SpiralThinker achieves state-of-the-art performance among latent reasoning baselines. Detailed analyses reveal that both iteration and alignment are indispensable, the numbers of latent tokens and iterations exhibit dataset-specific optima, and appropriate alignment proves critical for an effective iterative process. Overall, SpiralThinker bridges iterative computation and latent reasoning, demonstrating that aligned iterative updates can reliably steer reasoning in the latent space.
